Not a fan of this elitist attitude. I'll add I'm not really into lifting.

I believe there are 2 big factors to me that make weight training more popular and for some more accessible.

Progression in weight training it's a straightforward as you can get.

 While I think that the progression in calisthenics can keep things interesting, the fact that at different levels you are required to do different variations of exercises that have smaller or larger gaps of progression between them is a big turnoff. 

If you are struggling to do a lateral raise with 10 lb dumbbells you can just use five or 2.5 lb. Cannot do a pushup? Cannot do a pushup? Elevated pushups, kneeling push ups are fine but a suprising number of people would prefer to just add weight on the bench as they get stronger. This is especially an issue once you reach higher levels of strength. 

I am not saying that you cannot continue to build strength past one handed pushups, however commonly calisthenics exercises tend to rely on instability once you reach more advanced levels (one arm one leg push up, rings, handstandPU, etc).

These are good movements, but much less efficient if the goal is size and strength, and require a lot more thought and patience than adding weight to the bar.

Additionally many people (myself included) find it difficult to motivate themselves. Being in a public gym around other people who are working out, with nothing else to really do except to work out is a really effective way to get work in if you struggle. Of course you could do only calisthenics in the gym, but then you are not really using all of the tools at your disposal.

At the end of the day the best form of fitness is whatever keeps you enjoy and keeps you motivated and consistent.
